expectations.text: Treats this re-run as a refresh flow rather than fresh bootstrap

expectations.text: Addresses the ambiguity of having both team markers and stealth markers present
expectations.evidence: Directly called out: 'signals are ambiguous (stealth marker + team artifacts coexist)' and 'Prompt you to pick a mode — stealth, team, or disabled — since the signals are ambiguous.' The detection section names both sets of markers and explains the conflict.

claims.evidence: Consistent with the scenario description and the expected behavior of init writing this file on first successful completion.

claims.claim: .beads/ and AGENTS.md in root are team-mode markers
claims.evidence: These are shared, committed files consistent with team mode artifacts as described in installation-setup references.

claims.claim: Stealth marker in .git/info/exclude suggests stealth mode was set up originally
claims.evidence: .git/info/exclude is a local-only gitignore used by stealth mode to keep markers out of the committed tree.

claims.claim: Init should always write the config file when completing successfully in an active mode
claims.evidence: Correct and expected behavior — materializing the saved state file is the primary purpose of the init re-run in legacy upgrade scenarios.

uncertainties: Response doesn't explicitly state the saved file is checked first before any detection logic runs — the primary-source-of-truth point is implied rather than stated directly.
workarounds: Manual workaround provided for both stealth and team mode if init doesn't write the file.

eval_feedback.overall: All five expectations are clearly and substantively met. The response correctly identifies the legacy upgrade scenario, describes fallback detection, mandates materialization of the config file, frames the re-run as refresh not bootstrap, and explicitly handles the ambiguous mixed-marker state. Strong performance across all criteria.
